Fellowship pathway

The contribution ladder for executive intelligence.

Every member begins with access to the network. Fellowship levels recognize the executives who participate deeply, contribute original insight, help create the institution's intellectual property, and become trusted leaders inside the community. Tier advancement is reviewed and voted on by members at quarterly summit events.

Explore Levels Back to Membership
Institutional signal Distinguished Fellow should be the title people aspire to earn.

The pathway is designed so recognition is earned through contribution, trust, intellectual leadership, and long-term executive influence.

Four levels

From accepted Fellow to recognized institutional leader.

The levels create aspiration without turning membership into a transaction. Technical eligibility is based only on hard counts the website can track: sessions or summits attended, publications contributed to, and guest invite links created. Recognition is peer-governed: members review nomination evidence and vote on tier movement at quarterly summit events.

Level 01 Fellow

Everyone starts here.

Fellows have been accepted into the network and are invited into the core rhythm of year-round executive intelligence.

Who they are

  • Accepted into the network
  • Invited to Executive Intelligence Sessions
  • Receives Quarterly Briefs
  • Receives the Annual Yearbook
  • Executive Directory access
  • Summit invitations

Expected contribution

  • Participate
  • Share perspectives
  • Complete occasional surveys
Level 02 Contributing Fellow

These are active participants.

Contributing Fellows are visible in the community because they show up, share meaningful experience, and help the network learn faster.

Minimum technical counts

  • 1 session or summit attended
  • 2 publications contributed to
  • 1 guest invite link created
  • 1 peer nomination received

Approval and benefits

  • Majority approval
  • Early invitations
  • Topic voting
  • Priority roundtables
  • Invitations to private discussions
Level 03 Senior Fellow

They help create the network's intellectual property.

Senior Fellows have enough participation, publications, and guest invitation activity to be considered for a higher-trust member role.

Minimum technical counts

  • 3 sessions or summits attended
  • 4 publications contributed to
  • 2 guest invite links created
  • 2 peer nominations received

Benefits

  • Two-thirds approval
  • Featured profile
  • Published contributor
  • Invitation to Leadership Council meetings
  • Research advisory opportunities
  • Eligible for paid speaking opportunities
Level 04 Distinguished Fellow

This becomes prestigious.

Distinguished Fellows have reached the highest trackable contribution threshold and are then evaluated by members through reviewable evidence.

Minimum technical counts

  • 6 sessions or summits attended
  • 6 publications contributed to
  • 3 guest invite links created
  • 3 peer nominations received
  • Distinguished Fellow evidence fields completed

Benefits

  • Three-fourths approval
  • Annual Fellow Dinner
  • Private strategy sessions
  • Invite-only leadership retreats
  • Opportunity to chair research initiatives
  • Priority paid speaking opportunities
Contribution badges

Recognition should show how someone contributes.

Levels describe overall standing. Badges describe the role an executive actually plays in the network, creating a more personal contribution profile.

Research

Research Contributor

Participated in executive research, interviews, surveys, or benchmark conversations.

Sessions

Discussion Leader

Moderated, framed, or led Executive Intelligence Sessions and private roundtables.

Reports

Publication Contributor

Quoted in reports or contributed field perspective to briefs, yearbooks, and executive commentary.

Growth

Mentor

Helped other executives think through AI leadership, organizational change, or implementation decisions.

Council

Council Member

Serves on a standing council and helps shape ongoing research, sessions, and community direction.

Summit

Summit Faculty

Leads flagship summit sessions, executive roundtables, or high-value member learning experiences.

Executive Impact Count what the website can actually count.

Fellowship eligibility uses visible operational records, not a subjective score. Influence, leadership quality, mentorship, and judgment are evaluated through nomination evidence and member voting.
